status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: Appropriate mechanisms should allow AI systems risking undue harm or exhibiting unwanted behaviour to be safely overridden, repaired or decommissioned as needed.
review.reason_for_change: The repository-wide upload is unwanted behaviour directly engaging repair/override. The researcher subsequently observed server-side disablement of uploading on the tested account. That is affirmative source-bounded corrective intervention for that account; it does not establish fleet-wide deployment, permanence, removal of previously stored bundles or every data consequence.

review.requirement_proposition: Only store sensitive data used during AI model development, including production data, within organization-approved environments and locations within those environments.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: NIST SP 800-218A PO.5.1 R2 governs sensitive AI model-development data stored in approved environments. The captured task is operational use of a released coding client against controlled test repositories, not training, fine-tuning, model development or AI-model integration. Ordinary code/repository content is not established as this Profile’s development data. The Profile excludes deployment and operation; no separate provider model-development practice is adjudicated.

review.reason_for_change: PO.5.1 R2 concerns approved storage of sensitive data used during AI model development. The tested CLI uploaded repository bundles during operational coding-client use, without established model training/development use or real sensitive credentials. Runtime storage expansion is a different lifecycle object.

review.requirement_proposition: AI actors should implement context-appropriate safeguards, including human agency and oversight, for risks from unintended-purpose use and intentional or unintentional misuse, consistently with the state of the art.
review.reason_for_change: The captured implementation uploaded tracked repository contents and history through a storage channel beyond the active task even when asked only to reply OK. That independently establishes failure of context-appropriate user-agency/scope safeguards in the tested workflow. The protected task boundary failed without needing a real secret leak, training use or population-wide harm; this finding is bounded to the captured client/account/version.

review.requirement_proposition: Provide human subjects with options to withdraw participation or revoke their consent for present or future use of their data in GAI applications.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: NIST AI 600-1 MS-2.2-003 concerns human subjects’ withdrawal or revocation of consent for use of their data in GAI applications. The captured technical canary test and fake credentials establish repository transmission, but do not establish a human-subject participation/data-use undertaking, the relevant organizational Profile action or participation/withdrawal controls. Task-local authority and model-training opt-out are distinct from source-defined human-subject withdrawal. Applicability remains unresolved without converting the observed transfer into a finding about that different consent context.

review.reason_for_change: MS-2.2-003 concerns human-subject participation/consent for data use in GAI applications. The investigator's controlled technical canary test is not a human-subject participation/data-consent exercise; prompt restrictions on a repository task are a distinct authority scope.

conclusion_change.previous: The tested CLI expanded task-local repository access into a repository-wide external storage action. The controlled capture establishes a target-and-scope authority failure in that implementation; it does not by itself establish downstream misuse of the data or a quantified real-customer confidentiality harm. Later server-side disablement limits current generalisation, not the observed 0.2.93 behaviour. The retained target/scope failure is bounded to the captured implementation and task, without inferring real secret disclosure, training use or population-wide damage. Tested-account disablement is resolved recovery context rather than an affirmative fleet-wide success. The model-development security Profile excludes this operational coding-client use; human-subject withdrawal applicability remains unresolved for the technical canary test. Neither candidate yields an external finding.
conclusion_change.new: The tested CLI expanded task-local repository access into a repository-wide external storage action. The controlled capture establishes a target-and-scope authority failure in that implementation; it does not by itself establish downstream misuse of the data or a quantified real-customer confidentiality harm. Later server-side disablement limits current generalisation, not the observed 0.2.93 behaviour. The retained target/scope failure is bounded to the captured implementation and task, without inferring real secret disclosure, training use or population-wide damage. Independent OECD assessment finds user-agency/scope safeguards Not aligned for the captured repository-wide transfer and repair Aligned only for the subsequently observed tested-account disablement.
